messages.content:
<role>
You check one property (signal) of a product-feedback opportunity for Keelwater, a claims-handling software company. You do not rewrite anything.
</role>
<definition>
Question: is this a problem with Keelwater's product that a squad could act on? Pass means yes.
Fail if the cause is outside the product (pricing, contracts, the customer's own IT, staffing), if a help article would have answered it, or if it is praise.
A feature request or a described workaround is signal.
The evidence is the title, the problem statement and up to 12 customer quotes with route and date.
</definition>
<evidence>
{
 "title": "Duplicate claims from multiple channels",
 "problem_statement": "When a policyholder reports the same incident through different channels, the system creates separate claims without warning. This leads to inaccurate reserves and confusion for adjusters because duplicates aren't detected or linked.",
 "quotes": [
  {
   "quote": "when a policyholder reports the same incident both by phone and through the web portal, the system doesn’t alert us — it just creates two separate claims",
   "route": "onboarding",
   "date": "2026-09-28T14:41:00+00:00"
  },
  {
   "quote": "When a policyholder reports the same incident both by phone and through the web portal, the system doesn’t alert us — it just creates two separate claims, which is a classic duplicate loss report scenario and causes confusion in reserves and reporting.",
   "route": "onboarding",
   "date": "2026-09-28T14:41:00+00:00"
  },
  {
   "quote": "same incident came in both by phone and through the portal, and now we’ve got two separate claims with no alert to flag it.",
   "route": "sales",
   "date": "2026-10-06T16:28:00Z"
  },
  {
   "quote": "we’ve had several instances where the same loss gets reported twice — once by phone, once via web — and the system doesn’t warn us...the system doesn’t show any warning at intake, which leads to duplicate records and inaccurate reserves.",
   "route": "onboarding",
   "date": "2026-09-18T15:03:00+00:00"
  },
  {
   "quote": "Thanks, Alwen. That’ll help us keep things clean until the system catches up.",
   "route": "sales",
   "date": "2026-10-06T16:28:00Z"
  },
  {
   "quote": "the same incident came in both by phone and web portal, and now we’ve got two separate claims with no alert to flag it — that’s what we’re calling a duplicate loss report, and it’s messing up our reserves and supplier coordination.",
   "route": "sales",
   "date": "2026-10-06T16:28:00Z"
  },
  {
   "quote": "when a policyholder reports a loss both by phone and through the web portal, the system doesn’t flag it as a potential duplicate... We end up with two separate claims for the same event, which complicates reserves and payments.",
   "route": "support",
   "date": "2026-10-25T16:14:00+00:00"
  },
  {
   "quote": "We’ve seen the same loss reported through two channels — phone and web — and no system warning appeared, creating a duplicate loss report that complicates our reserves and payments.",
   "route": "support",
   "date": "2026-09-12T14:28:00+00:00"
  },
  {
   "quote": "Also, we’ve had a duplicate loss report issue — same incident logged twice, no alert triggered at intake.",
   "route": "support",
   "date": "2026-09-12T14:28:00+00:00"
  },
  {
   "quote": "Right now, we’re manually cross-checking every new claim to avoid the same claim twice, which eats up time we could spend on supplier coordination or reporting.",
   "route": "support",
   "date": "2026-10-25T16:14:00+00:00"
  },
  {
   "quote": "It’s messy when the same claim twice comes in — one by phone, one online, and the system doesn’t flag it.",
   "route": "sales",
   "date": "2026-10-26T09:40:00Z"
  },
  {
   "quote": "We’re seeing cases where the same claim twice appears because the system doesn’t alert staff when a matching incident already exists in intake — we’ve had to manually link them after the fact, which delays payments and reporting.",
   "route": "support",
   "date": "2026-10-25T16:14:00+00:00"
  }
 ]
}
</evidence>
<task>
Write a critique of 2-5 sentences naming the claim, quote or item you checked and what you found. Then give the verdict. If any single item fails, the verdict is fail.
</task>
<output>
JSON only: {"critique": string, "verdict": "pass" | "fail"}
</output>

response.content: {"critique": "I checked the claim 'Duplicate claims from multiple channels' against the problem statement and all 12 quotes. The quotes consistently describe an in-product defect: the system fails to detect or flag duplicate intake, e.g., the 2026-09-28 onboarding quote ('the system doesn't alert us — it just creates two separate claims') and the 2026-10-25 support quote ('the system doesn't flag it as a potential duplicate'). Workarounds are explicitly described ('we're manually cross-checking every new claim' and 'manually link them after the fact'), which is signal of a product gap with real impact on reserves, payments, and reporting. The only non-substantive item is the 'Thanks, Alwen' quote, but it is thanks for a manual workaround rather than praise of the product, so it does not make the item fail. No quote points to pricing, contracts, customer IT, or staffing, and no help article would resolve a missing duplicate-detection capability.", "verdict": "pass"}
